basics.label: Professor of Herbology, Research Botanist & Field Operations Veteran
basics.name: Neville Longbottom
basics.summary: Highly accomplished Herbology scholar and internationally recognised experimental botanist with extensive experience in field research, species documentation, and operating in challenging, occasionally hazardous environments. Proven leader and decorated veteran, adept at independent work, problem-solving under pressure, and maintaining conviction in the face of scepticism. Expertise in magically-responsive plant cultivars, conservation of endangered wizarding flora, and the discovery and documentation of previously uncatalogued magical species. Former Auror with tactical field experience.

projects.description: A multi-institution conservation programme aimed at cataloguing, seed-banking, and cultivating endangered magical plant species. Partners include the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, the Beauxbatons Botanical Institute, and two Scandinavian magical natural history museums. This programme directly involves documentation and study of rare and unusual magical flora.
highlights: Catalogued 63 species of endangered magical flora across the Hogwarts grounds and surrounding region
Established a living seed bank of over 200 species in the Hogwarts greenhouse complex, including difficult-to-cultivate species
Developed propagation protocols for four species previously considered uncultivable in captivity
Trained twelve botanical researchers from partner institutions in magical plant handling and cultivation, demonstrating mentorship capabilities

publications.name: Mandrake Restorative Draught Potency: The Impact of Soil Composition and Maturation Rate
publications.summary: Research paper demonstrating that modifications to Mandrake cultivation soil composition and controlled maturation timing significantly improve the potency and reliability of the standard Restorative Draught formula. Adopted into revised St Mungo's treatment protocols. Exemplifies experimental research and practical application.

publications.name: Teaching Herbology to Traumatised Learners: A Framework for Post-Conflict Magical Education
publications.summary: Practitioner-focused paper drawing on Neville's experience teaching post-war students at Hogwarts, proposing a trauma-sensitive pedagogical framework applicable across magical subjects with particular relevance to Herbology's sensory and practical elements. Highlights adaptability and resilience in challenging teaching environments.

references.name: Harry Potter, Head Auror — Ministry of Magic
references.reference: Neville is one of the bravest people I've ever known — and I mean that in a specific, evidence-based way. He spent an entire year leading resistance against Death Eaters while the rest of us were on the run, took punishment that would have broken most adults, and then showed up for the Battle without hesitation. He destroyed the last Horcrux while I was supposed to be dead. That sort of person, you don't forget. As a professor he's exceptional — every student who's come through his Herbology class comes out of it actually caring about the subject. His conviction and ability to act under duress are unparalleled.

references.name: Professor Minerva McGonagall, Headmistress — Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
references.reference: Professor Longbottom has exceeded every expectation I had when I appointed him, and my expectations were already high. He has built the Herbology programme into one of the finest in Britain while simultaneously serving as an exemplary Head of House. His commitment to student welfare — particularly to students who carry the weight of the war years — reflects the very best of Gryffindor values. His transformation into a resilient and respected figure exemplifies his enduring strength of character.
